requirements.text: Preserve read/write semantics while scaling hot reads.
Move long jobs off the request path with stable job identity.
Bound stale reads, retries and overload without claiming exactly-once side effects.

problem.scope: Progress from a low-latency query/update service to cache and background execution. Compare transactional cache-aside with command-log/read-model separation; target QPS is a workload assumption, not measured capacity.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Transactions isolate concurrent authorization and mutation decisions; retries remain explicit.

references.title: HTTP caching

acceptanceCases.then: Retain one job identity and refuse the stale result commit.
acceptanceCases.when: Retry the same request ID and run two lease owners.

acceptanceCases.given: A session requires version 8 but the replica has version 7.
acceptanceCases.then: Use primary or return explicit not-yet-available; never silently return version 7.

acceptanceCases.given: A bounded job map is initially empty.
acceptanceCases.then: Admit one intent, deduplicate exact repeat, reject the conflict.
acceptanceCases.when: Admit the same ID/hash twice then conflicting bytes.

guarantees: Cache hit does not imply read-your-write unless a minimum version is enforced.
An insufficient replica version cannot satisfy a strong session read.
An expired owner cannot commit over its successor.
A unique local row alone cannot deduplicate a remote webhook.
Overload is surfaced rather than hidden in unbounded queues.

apis.errors: Reject invalid input, stale versions and operations outside the declared boundary.

solutions.chooseWhen: A relational write authority meets the load and eventual hot-read freshness is acceptable.

stages.explanation: Preserve read/write semantics while scaling hot reads. [An API contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_programming_interface) states what callers send, what an outcome means, and how failures are reported. It should remain clear before the implementation is split into more components. Consider this case: A job request times out after its intent commits. Retry the same request ID and run two lease owners.
invariants: Preserve read/write semantics while scaling hot reads.
stages.question: What does successful completion promise?
stages.reason: Preserve read/write semantics while scaling hot reads.
stages.title: Define the operation boundary

stages.explanation: Authorize requests and commit versioned updates at one write authority. Own records, versions and durable job intent. request context belongs to Stateless API; object rows and job keys belongs to Primary database. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.
invariants: request context belongs to Stateless API; object rows and job keys belongs to Primary database.
stages.question: Which component owns the decision and its persistent or shared state?
stages.reason: Authorize requests and commit versioned updates at one write authority. Own records, versions and durable job intent.
stages.title: Expose authority and state

stages.explanation: Read a versioned cached value or fill from authority; updates invalidate after commit with bounded TTL. Cache hit does not imply read-your-write unless a minimum version is enforced. [A cache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache_replacement_policies) keeps reusable results in limited memory. Eviction controls space, while ownership and invalidation rules determine whether a returned value is still safe to use.
invariants: Cache hit does not imply read-your-write unless a minimum version is enforced.

operations.reason: Expose this new typed path without mutating earlier binding definitions.

stages.question: How are hot reads removed from the primary?
stages.reason: Read a versioned cached value or fill from authority; updates invalidate after commit with bounded TTL.
stages.title: Versioned read cache

stages.explanation: Serve only reads whose required version is available; route stronger reads to primary. An insufficient replica version cannot satisfy a strong session read. [Replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replication_%28computing%29) keeps copies of state on multiple nodes. Copying data alone does not decide which copy may accept writes or how much stale data a read may return.
invariants: An insufficient replica version cannot satisfy a strong session read.
stages.question: When is replica lag acceptable?
stages.reason: Serve only reads whose required version is available; route stronger reads to primary.
stages.title: Replica reader

stages.explanation: Insert job identity and input hash with the business transaction before returning accepted. Accepted does not mean completed. [A transaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_transaction) commits related state changes together or leaves them unapplied. The database must enforce the relevant condition during the write, rather than trusting an earlier read. Consider this case: A job request times out after its intent commits.

operations.reason: Expose this new typed path without mutating earlier binding definitions.

stages.question: How is a long task accepted durably?
stages.reason: Insert job identity and input hash with the business transaction before returning accepted.
stages.title: Job outbox

stages.explanation: Claim bounded work, run with a lease epoch, and retain the original job ID on retry. An expired owner cannot commit over its successor. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources. A newer owner needs a token that the resource checks, not merely a belief that ownership changed.
invariants: An expired owner cannot commit over its successor.
stages.question: What happens after worker loss?
stages.reason: Claim bounded work, run with a lease epoch, and retain the original job ID on retry.
stages.title: Leased worker

stages.explanation: Commit one result identity per job and model external effects with their own deduplication contract. A unique local row alone cannot deduplicate a remote webhook. [Idempotence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence) means repeating the same logical operation does not repeat its effect. Stable request identities let a retry recover an existing outcome instead of creating another change.
invariants: A unique local row alone cannot deduplicate a remote webhook.
stages.question: Can retry publish two results?
stages.reason: Commit one result identity per job and model external effects with their own deduplication contract.
stages.title: Idempotent result

stages.explanation: Reject or defer when per-tenant queued work or database concurrency reaches its declared bound. Overload is surfaced rather than hidden in unbounded queues. [Backpressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_control_%28data%29) prevents producers from outrunning the next component indefinitely. The design must choose whether excess work waits, is rejected, or is dropped with an explicit outcome. Consider this case: A job request times out after its intent commits.
invariants: Overload is surfaced rather than hidden in unbounded queues.

operations.reason: Expose this new typed path without mutating earlier binding definitions.

stages.question: What prevents a backlog collapse?
stages.reason: Reject or defer when per-tenant queued work or database concurrency reaches its declared bound.
stages.title: Admission budget

solutions.title: Cache-aside API and job outbox
tradeoffs: Invalidation races need versioned entries or a bounded staleness promise.

stages.explanation: Validate authenticated commands and append stable command identity. Own immutable ordered commands and deduplication receipts. accepted command offset belongs to Command admission; per-aggregate sequence belongs to Command journal. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version.
invariants: accepted command offset belongs to Command admission; per-aggregate sequence belongs to Command journal.

stages.reason: Validate authenticated commands and append stable command identity. Own immutable ordered commands and deduplication receipts.

stages.explanation: Apply one aggregate sequence with expected-version checks and atomic checkpoint. Conflicting commands fail explicitly instead of silently overwriting. [A checkpoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkpointing) records enough progress to restart without repeating everything. Its usefulness depends on which state is durable and whether later effects can be replayed safely. Consider this case: A reducer replays the same accepted command. Emit its long-task intent twice.
invariants: Conflicting commands fail explicitly instead of silently overwriting.

The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters. Consider this case: A reducer replays the same accepted command. Emit its long-task intent twice.
invariants: A projection names its freshness boundary.

[A control loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_loop) compares desired state with observed state and applies corrections. Repeated execution must converge safely, especially when a previous action succeeded but its reply was lost. Consider this case: A reducer replays the same accepted command. Emit its long-task intent twice.
invariants: Unknown external outcome remains unknown until reconciled.

stages.reason: Consume stable IDs with leased retries and explicit external idempotency/reconciliation.
stages.title: Task runner

stages.explanation: Replay into a shadow projection and publish only after its target offset is reached. Clients do not mix two projection generations. [An event log](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Event-driven_architecture) preserves ordered changes so a consumer can rebuild state or catch up. The consumer must remember its position and handle repeated delivery without repeated effects. Consider this case: A reducer replays the same accepted command.
invariants: Clients do not mix two projection generations.

stages.reason: Replay into a shadow projection and publish only after its target offset is reached.
